cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Generate a larger set of options by scaling the test set\nvoid generateOptions(std::vector<OptionInput>& options, const size_t numOptions) {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    options.resize(numOptions);\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numOptions; ++i) {\n        // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n        const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n        options[i] = base;\n        \n        // Add some variation for larger datasets\n        const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n        options[i].spot *= factor;\n        options[i].strike *= factor;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %d: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfyWPayEX5AqVPzCVedCJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark is now a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. It builds cleanly and runs on the 4× RTX 3090 node, and the numerical results agree with the original to about 1e-13 relative. The bit-exact hash does not match the original, though. The reason is covered below.\n\n**What changed** (only `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt`):\n\n- **MPI:** Each rank prices a contiguous block of option indices. Results are gathered in index order on rank 0, so the sum, min, max, and hash run over the same sequence as before. Output is printed by rank 0 only, and all ranks exit with the same status.\n- **OpenMP:** Each rank drives the GPUs assigned to it, with one OpenMP thread per device. Ranks on a node split the GPUs; if there are more ranks than GPUs, ranks share them.\n- **CUDA:** One kernel computes each option from its global index, using the same arithmetic as the original `generateOptions`. Only results cross the PCIe bus. The formula is shared between host and device code.\n- **CMake:** The `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA source, so no new files were needed. MPI, OpenMP, and CUDA are all `REQUIRED`, so there is no fallback path. The executable name is unchanged.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Built with no warnings. The output includes the same header, sample, and validation lines as before.\n- Output matches across 1, 2, and 4 ranks, with the same hash and sum. Validation passes.\n- The original build's reference hash (`a1819ec14da95077`) is reproduced by a host-formula harness, which I used to compare device prices with the original math.\n- Edge cases work: N=0, N smaller than the rank count, `-h`, unknown options, and exit codes.\n\n**Performance (N = 10⁸):** The original runs at about 11 million options/s (9.1 s). The hybrid build runs at about 1.2–1.8 billion options/s, depending on rank count. Timing covers the pricing phase only, from the barrier to the results being in host memory; the gather is outside the timer.\n\n**Numerical difference:** Some hashes differ from the original, and I did not hide that. On the device, `erf`/`exp`/`log` come from CUDA's `libm`, not glibc. About 68% of prices are bit-identical. The rest differ by up to 2.8e-13 relative, mostly in deep out-of-the-money cases where the formula cancels. Turning off FMA on either side does not fix it. Bit-identical hashes would require reimplementing glibc's math on the GPU. Validation tolerances are far looser than this, so I kept the native device math.\n\n**Choices you may want to revisit:**\n- `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` is `all-major`, not `native`. The installed nvcc is 12.0, which does not support `native`, and without it CMake silently generated `compute_52`. `all-major` makes a larger binary and a slower compile, but runs on any cluster GPU. Set `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` if you want a single-architecture build.\n- Option count is limited to `INT_MAX` (about 2.1 billion), because MPI gather counts are `int`. The program rejects larger values with an error.\n- CMake's minimum version was raised from 3.10 to 3.23 for the CUDA language support.\n\nI left `output.txt` alone; it is a session transcript, not part of the build. My test binaries and harness are in `/tmp`, not in the repo."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2043,"cache_read_input_tokens":74224,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2043},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e225be45-989f-4242-8fa9-0b8f8bdfc2ae","uuid":"247dbc37-ef47-43a6-a916-3c83ca2ac433","timestamp":"2026-10-13T03:14:13.182Z","request_id":"req_011CfyWPaNmWMJq9C3GcdLgv"}
